title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (§41, Longue Marche sequel). The question is which outer automorphisms of the profinite group π̂_{0,3} = π̂_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) can come from Π_Q = Gal(Q̄/Q). Earlier pages set up congruence conditions (§38). Here Grothendieck looks for a further necessary condition, built from a second structure on π_{0,3}.

(1)–(2) Let π_{0,3} = ⟨ℓ_0, ℓ_1, ℓ_∞ | product = 1⟩, which is free on two generators. Kill ℓ_1^2 and ℓ_∞^3. The quotient π'_{0,3} = π_{0,3}/⟨⟨ℓ_1^2, ℓ_∞^3⟩⟩ is Z/2 * Z/3 ≅ PSL_2(Z). This is the 'oriented triangulated cartographic group' of the Esquisse: the oriented cartographic group with the extra relation that faces are triangles.

It is identified with G^+_{0,3} ≅ π_1^orb((U_{0,3}^an, S_3), P), the orbifold fundamental group of the S_3-quotient (P^1−{0,1,∞})/S_3. Via λ ↦ j this quotient is the j-line orbifold, essentially M_{1,1} rigidified by ±1.

The composite φ is given by the 'brutal formulas' φ(ℓ_0) = σ_∞ρ, φ(ℓ_1) = σ_∞ (order 2), φ(ℓ_∞) = ρ^{-1} (order 3).

(3) Profinite completion gives an epimorphism φ̂ : π̂_{0,3} → Ĝ^+_{0,3} = π_1((U_{0,3,Q̄}, S_3), P). Ĝ^+_{0,3} also contains π̂_{0,3} as a normal subgroup of index 6 (the other map, Γ(2)/±1 ⊂ PSL_2(Z)). Acting by conjugation, it embeds into the group of 'local' automorphisms of π̂_{0,3}, i.e. those respecting inertia classes up to permutation; this is the double-hat cartographic group.

So PSL_2(Z)^ meets π̂_{0,3} in two different ways: as a quotient (φ̂) and as an overgroup (S_3-orbifold).

Now take a subgroup Π ⊂ Aut ext'_loc(π̂_{0,3}) commuting with S_3 (e.g. the image of Galois, or a GT-type group). Π automatically acts as outer automorphisms on Ĝ^+_{0,3}, through the extension (4) of the next page. The proposed new necessary condition is that φ̂ be Π-equivariant, i.e. that it fit into a morphism of extensions. On the next page Grothendieck calls this 'a priori a non-trivial condition', element by element, to be made explicit like the congruence conditions.

Geometrically, φ̂ is the map on π_1 induced by the open immersion of P^1−{0,1,∞} into the orbifold P^1 with cusp at 0, a Z/2-point at 1 and a Z/3-point at ∞. That orbifold is the j-line M_{1,1}/±1 in the coordinate t = 1728/j, which is defined over Q.
errors: Consistency of (2) depends on the orientation convention. With ℓ_0ℓ_1ℓ_∞ = 1 the images give σ_∞ρσ_∞ρ^{-1}, which is not 1 in Z/2*Z/3. With ℓ_0ℓ_∞ℓ_1 = 1 (equivalently ℓ_1ℓ_0ℓ_∞ = 1) one gets σ_∞ρρ^{-1}σ_∞ = σ_∞^2 = 1. So the formulas presuppose the latter convention, presumably that of [C].

Equivariance under Gal(Q̄/Q) itself is not a genuinely new restriction. φ̂ is induced by the Q-rational open immersion of P^1−{0,1,∞} into the j-line orbifold, so it is automatically Galois-equivariant as an outer homomorphism. The condition only cuts down a candidate group Π (e.g. GT-type). The page does not note this geometric origin; whether later pages do is unknown.

ideas.what: π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) modulo ℓ_1^2, ℓ_∞^3 is Z/2*Z/3 = PSL_2(Z), the oriented cartographic group of triangulated maps
ideas.modern_name: PSL_2(Z) as cartographic group of triangulations / orbifold π_1 of M_{1,1}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse); classical for the group theory
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (cartographic groups, PSL_2(Z) for triangulations)

ideas.what: Ĝ^+_{0,3} as orbifold π_1 of the S_3-quotient of U_{0,3}, containing π̂_{0,3} with index 6 and acting on it by 'local' automorphisms
ideas.modern_name: π̂_1(M_{0,4}/S_3) ≅ PSL_2(Z)^ ⊃ Γ(2)^; S_3-extended GT setting

ideas.what: Test equivariance of the epimorphism π̂_{0,3} → PSL_2(Z)^ under a candidate group of outer automorphisms, as a further necessary condition for coming from Gal(Q̄/Q) beyond congruence conditions
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of GT-type actions with π_1 of M_{1,1} / genus-one GT conditions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps (1997), Nakamura; GT action on B_3^/Z = PSL_2(Z)^ via Drinfeld

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes making explicit, element by element, the condition that an outer automorphism of π̂_{0,3} commuting with S_3 be compatible with the quotient map π̂_{0,3} → (Z/2*Z/3)^ = PSL_2(Z)^. This is a 'quotient-side' companion to the usual S_3/overgroup condition defining GT. In GT parameters (λ, f) it would be a condition that f respect the relations x^2, y^3 after a change of generators.
missed.quote: Cet homomorphisme est défini ici par les "formules brutales" (2), sans référence à un sous-groupe particulier Π de Aut ext'_loc(π̂_{0,3})
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Galois satisfies it automatically: it is induced by the Q-rational open immersion into the j-line. Whether GT-hat satisfies it is a concrete question about GT vs Galois via the open embedding P^1−{0,1,∞} ⊂ [M_{1,1}]. This is related to, but not obviously identical with, the genus-one conditions of Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps.

deep.surprise_reason: The setup is natural and close to later work on GT and M_{1,1}/PSL_2(Z)^ actions. The explicit idea of using the epimorphism (not the index-6 inclusion) as a constraint on candidate Galois-type groups is an interesting unpublished angle. However, its content for Galois itself is automatic.
transcription_corrections: In (3) the subscript should read U_{0,3, Q̄} (base change to Q̄), not 'Q̄_0'.
In the line under (3), 'ext' in Aut ext_loc appears struck through or overwritten; it reads roughly Ĉ̂_{0,3} = Aut_loc(π̂_{0,3}). The ∩ sits under Ĝ^+_{0,3}, indicating its embedding into this group.
'(avec les notations de [C, ...] ...)' refers to the cartographic notes [C]; σ_∞ and ρ are generators of the cartographic group.
